topic: India-Canada Relations: Reset, CEPA and Strains

subtopics.title: Background of Bilateral Ties
subtopics.summary: India and Canada established diplomatic ties in 1947 and cooperate in trade, nuclear energy and space. Bilateral trade was worth USD 30.9 billion in 2024. Their nuclear and space links date back to the 1950s and 2013.
facts: Diplomatic ties established in 1947.
Bilateral trade worth USD 30.9 billion in 2024.
Nuclear Cooperation Agreement (2013) facilitates uranium supply and oversight.
Canada assisted India in building a nuclear research reactor named CIRUS in 1954.
Space collaboration between ISRO and the Canadian Space Agency.
Joint research collaboration exists between the two countries.

subtopics.title: Key Outcomes of the Canadian PM's Visit
subtopics.summary: Canadian PM Mark Carney signalled a reset with India, and formal CEPA trade talks restarted. The visit produced outcomes in energy, climate, technology, agriculture, student mobility and critical minerals. Several outcomes came with a stated target or time frame.
facts: Negotiations on CEPA formally restarted.
Bilateral trade target set at $50 billion by 2030.
Canada's Cameco to supply uranium ore concentrates from 2027 to 2035.
Canada announced intent to join the International Solar Alliance.
Canada to upgrade to full membership in the Global Biofuels Alliance.
ACITI (Australia-Canada-India Technology and Innovation) Partnership launched.
ACITI focus: emerging technologies, digital innovation, advanced manufacturing.
Pulse Protein Centre of Excellence set up at National Institute of Food Technology Entrepreneurship and Management.
Fully funded research internships for 300 Indian students annually.
MoU signed for secure and resilient critical minerals supply chains, aligned with the G7 Critical Minerals Action Plan.

subtopics.title: Diplomatic Strains and Trade Impact
subtopics.summary: Ties deteriorated after PM Justin Trudeau alleged a potential link between Indian agents and the 2023 killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar. Both countries expelled diplomats and froze consular services. The rifts stalled CEPA talks, slowed trade and delayed visa processing.
facts: PM Justin Trudeau alleged a potential link between Indian agents and Nijjar's killing in 2023.
Both countries expelled diplomats and froze consular services.
India sees Canada's tolerance of Khalistani separatist groups as a threat to territorial integrity.
Diplomatic rifts stalled CEPA negotiations and slowed bilateral trade.
Diplomatic rifts created uncertainty about Canadian investments in India.
Delays in Canadian visa processing for Indians due to reduced Canadian diplomatic staff.
The standoff may harm India's G20 reputation.
The standoff may complicate relations with Five Eyes allies and a G7 member.

subtopics.title: Khalistan Movement and Its Context
subtopics.summary: The Khalistan movement is rooted in Sikh identity, the 1947 Partition and demands for Punjab's autonomy. Violent episodes such as the Air India bombing and the 1984 assassination of Indira Gandhi shaped the issue. Diaspora-based separatist support abroad keeps the issue alive in India-Canada ties.
facts: Khalsa tradition established in 1699, marking Sikh identity and autonomy.
Partition of India (1947) left Sikhs as a minority, creating dissatisfaction over lost ancestral lands.
Anandpur Sahib Resolution demanded greater autonomy for Punjab.
Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale became the face of Sikh militancy, advocating Khalistan.
Operation Black Thunder: Indian forces removed militants from the Golden Temple.
Air India bombing: Canada-based Sikh extremists bombed a flight.
In 1984, Indira Gandhi's Sikh bodyguards killed her, triggering anti-Sikh riots.
Khalistani groups found support in Canada, the UK, the US and Australia.

subtopics.title: Vienna Conventions on Diplomatic Immunity
subtopics.summary: The Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations (1961) and the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations (1963) set the framework for diplomatic and consular ties. They protect diplomats from arrest and legal processes and make diplomatic missions inviolable. Consular officers can perform their duties without interference.
facts: Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations (1961) sets the framework for diplomatic relations.
Vienna Convention on Consular Relations (1963) sets the framework for consular relations.
Diplomats are protected from arrest and legal processes (diplomatic immunity).
Missions cannot be entered without permission (inviolability of diplomatic premises).
Consular officers can perform duties without interference.
Diplomatic immunity is the key provision protecting diplomats.

quizzes.passage: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney visited India and signalled a reset in the relationship between the two countries. The reset came after a period of strained ties between the two countries. The visit led to a formal restart of negotiations on the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, known as CEPA. Cooperation was also widened in several areas. In energy, a Canadian company agreed to supply uranium ore concentrates to India, which supports India's fuel security. On climate and energy, Canada announced its intention to join a major solar alliance. In technology, a trilateral partnership was launched to promote innovation across the three countries. In agriculture, a centre of excellence was set up to work on pulse-based food products. Student mobility was a key theme of the visit, as education links continue to grow. Students and research ties also received attention, with research internships planned for Indian students. Finally, a memorandum of understanding was signed to build secure supply chains in critical minerals. Bilateral trade is an important part of the relationship, and both sides want it to grow further. The outcomes cover trade, energy, technology, agriculture and people-to-people links. Taken together, these outcomes show how the two countries plan to move beyond trade into new areas of partnership.

quizzes.passage: Relations between India and Canada came under strain after a series of disputes. Diplomatic ties between the two countries had been in place since 1947, so the strain was felt in a long-established relationship. Canada's Prime Minister alleged a possible link between Indian agents and the killing of a Sikh separatist leader, Hardeep Singh Nijjar. The disagreement deepened when both countries expelled diplomats and froze consular services, which made it harder for citizens to access official help. Routine services for citizens became harder to obtain for a time. India viewed Canada's tolerance of separatist groups as a threat to its territorial integrity, and this added to the mistrust between the two governments. The rifts also reached the economy. Trade negotiations were halted, bilateral trade slowed and investors in India were left facing uncertainty. Business planning became harder because of the uncertainty around trade ties and new investment in the region. Students and job applicants felt the impact as visa processing for Indians became slower. The standoff was also seen as a risk to India's standing in major global forums and to its ties with some of Canada's closest partners. Taken together, these developments show how a single dispute can spread into trade, visas and wider diplomacy.
